title: Computational modeling and characterization methods for rotating magnetic nanochain-enhanced lateral flow immunoassays☆☆☆
author: Orlov, Malkerov, et al.

steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect functionalized magnetic nanochains, target antigen (e.g., H‑FABP), running buffer (PBS pH 7.4 with 10 % v/v antigen‑free pooled human serum, 1 % w/v BSA, 0.1 % v/v Tween‑20), a neodymium N52 permanent magnet (≥0.3 T surface field), micropipettes (10–100 µL), 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, lateral flow test strips, and for SEM: nitrocellulose membranes, sputter coater, gold target, SEM instrument.

steps.title: Prepare antigen solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the target antigen in running buffer to a known concentration (e.g., 1.0 ng mL⁻¹). Aliquot 50 µL of this solution into each 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, preparing at least three replicates for every experimental condition.

steps.title: Add magnetic nanochains
steps.instruction: To each tube add the predetermined amount of functionalized magnetic nanochains (e.g., 3 µg). Include a control tube that receives no nanochains.

steps.title: Incubate with or without rotation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 6 min at room temperature under the following conditions: (a) Rotation – place the tube on a device that generates a rotating magnetic field of 3 Hz frequency and 200 Oe field strength; (b) Static – keep the tube stationary with no magnetic field; (c) Control – tube without nanochains, also kept static.

steps.title: Magnetic separation and supernatant collection
steps.instruction: After incubation, place each tube against a strong permanent magnet for 2 min to sediment the nanochains against the tube wall. Carefully pipette 40 µL of the clear supernatant without disturbing the pellet and transfer it to a clean tube for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quantify residual antigen
steps.instruction: Measure the antigen concentration in each supernatant sample using a lateral flow assay (or an equivalent quantitative method). Prepare a calibration curve from known antigen standards and run all measurements in triplicate.

steps.title: Calculate capture efficiency and improvement
steps.instruction: For each condition compute capture efficiency % = [(C₀ – Cₛ)/C₀] × 100, where C₀ is the initial 1.0 ng mL⁻¹ and Cₛ is the measured supernatant concentration. Then calculate fold improvement = (efficiency with rotation) / (efficiency without rotation).

steps.title: Prepare membrane groups for SEM
steps.instruction: Cut nitrocellulose membrane pieces (5 mm × 5 mm). Assign three groups: (i) unused control membranes, (ii) membranes used in standard lateral‑flow assays without magnetic field, (iii) membranes exposed to magnetic rotation (3 Hz, 200 Oe) during a 6‑minute assay.

steps.title: Air‑dry and sputter‑coat membranes
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the membrane pieces for 24 h at room temperature. Then sputter‑coat each piece with a 5 nm gold film (99.9 % purity) using a cold‑magnetron sputter coater set to 50 mTorr chamber pressure, 10 mA target current, for approximately 15 min.

steps.title: Image membranes by SEM
steps.instruction: Place the coated membranes in a Tescan MAIA3 field‑emission SEM. Image at 20 kV accelerating voltage, 4.99 mm working distance, 3270 × magnification (field of view 63.5 µm) using the in‑beam secondary‑electron detector to capture surface topography.
